Why "4" Cells Are Your Best Friend

A wall cell numbered "4" is the strongest clue in any Akari puzzle — all four adjacent cells must contain a cat, no thinking required. Start every puzzle by scanning for 4s first. Then check if those cats illuminate enough cells to reveal new forced placements. This "cascade from 4s" technique works on every difficulty level and is the single fastest way to speed up your solving.

What is GridPaw? — Free Akari Puzzle Game

GridPaw is a free Light Up puzzle game with charming cats. Your goal is to place glowing cats on the grid so that every empty cell is illuminated, while respecting the numbered clues. It's the same satisfying logic as Akari puzzles — a classic Japanese brain teaser — but wrapped in an adorable feline theme.

Whether you're a puzzle veteran or completely new to Akari, GridPaw offers a gentle learning curve: start with the Tutorial, work through Easy boards, and graduate to Expert and Master sizes up to 12×12. Every level is hand-crafted and solvable with pure logic — no guessing required.

How Akari Puzzles Work

The rules of Akari (Light Up) are simple to learn but hard to master:

  • Place lights (glowing cats) on empty cells.
  • Lights illuminate their entire row and column until blocked by a wall.
  • No two lights may shine on each other — if two cats can see each other in the same row or column, that's illegal.
  • Numbered cells indicate exactly how many lights must be placed directly adjacent (up, down, left, right).
  • The puzzle is solved when every empty cell is lit and every numbered clue is satisfied.

How to Play Akari Puzzle — GridPaw Guide

Tap any empty cell to place a glowing cat. Tap again to remove it. The top bar shows your remaining lives — make an invalid move and you'll lose one. Use the Hint button when you're stuck: it reveals the next logical cell without solving the entire board.

Double-click (or right-click / long-press on mobile) to mark a cell with a paw print — useful for noting cells you know can't have cats. This note-taking mechanic is essential for harder puzzles where you need to track multiple possibilities.

Each difficulty introduces gradually bigger boards: 5×5 for Tutorial, 6×6 for Easy, up to 12×12 for Master. Larger boards require more advanced Akari techniques, including edge reasoning and exclusion along walls, but the core mechanic never changes.

Akari Puzzle Difficulty Levels Explained

  • Tutorial (5×5) — Perfect for first-timers. Small grid, simple clues, quick wins. Teaches every rule step by step.
  • Easy (6×6) — Great for building confidence. More numbered clues, straightforward deduction.
  • Medium (7×7) — The standard challenge. Requires intermediate techniques like line-of-sight elimination.
  • Medium-Hard (8×8) — Mixed layouts requiring careful scanning and cross-hatching.
  • Hard (9×9) — For experienced puzzlers. Fewer clues, deeper reasoning needed.
  • Expert (10×10) — Misplacement causes cascading errors. Plan before you place.
  • Master (12×12) — The ultimate challenge for the most demanding solvers.

Tips & Strategy for Akari Puzzles

Rushing to fill cells is the fastest way to lose lives. Instead, work systematically:

  1. Start with the 4s. A wall cell numbered 4 forces a light in every adjacent cell — no other option. Place them immediately.
  2. Use 0s next. A 0 means none of its neighbors can have cats. Mark them all with paw prints right away.
  3. Watch for "dead cells." If a cell can't be lit from any direction after a placement, that placement is wrong.
  4. Mark uncertain candidates. Use the paw print mark to track possibilities before committing.
  5. Validate lines, not cells. Check entire rows and columns for conflicts before finalizing a section.
  6. Look for forced placements. If a cell can only be lit from one direction, that's a forced cat position.

Once you internalize these patterns, you'll notice that advanced Akari boards are rarely about searching — they're about eliminating impossible positions until only one solution remains. Visit our Tips & Strategy page for detailed guides on each technique.

Common Akari Puzzle Mistakes to Avoid

New Akari puzzle players often make the same few mistakes. Forgetting line-of-sight: two cats in the same row or column without a wall between them is always illegal — the game will warn you with a shake animation. Ignoring number constraints: a numbered cell's count is exact, not "at most." A "2" needs exactly two cats adjacent, no more and no fewer. Guessing instead of deducing: every Akari puzzle in GridPaw has a unique solution that can be reached by pure logic. If you're guessing, you're missing a clue — try the Hint button to find the next logical step.

Akari Puzzle Tips for Advanced Players

Once you've mastered the basics, try these advanced Akari puzzle strategies. Corner tactics: a "2" in a corner means both adjacent cells must have cats — no guesswork needed. Forced lighting: if a white cell can only be reached by one possible cat position, that position is forced. Number propagation: when you know a number already has enough adjacent cats, mark its remaining neighbors as empty. Wall scanning: check each wall segment — if a row has only one unlit cell between two walls, that cell must hold a cat. These techniques are essential for Hard and Expert Akari puzzle grids.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is GridPaw free to play?
Yes, GridPaw is completely free to play in your browser. There is no download, no account, and no payment required. Just open the page and start solving.
What is an Akari (Light Up) puzzle?
Akari, also called Light Up, is a Japanese logic puzzle where you place lights so every empty cell is illuminated, while numbered cells tell you exactly how many adjacent lights they touch. GridPaw is the cat-themed version — place glowing cats instead of bulbs!
How is GridPaw different from Sudoku?
Both are logic puzzles, but the rules are very different. Sudoku fills a grid with numbers; GridPaw places glowing cats to light up the board. If you like Sudoku's deduction, you'll enjoy GridPaw's clue-based lighting. The spatial reasoning is a refreshing change from number crunching.
Where should beginners start?
Start with the Tutorial level, which walks you through every rule step by step, then move to Easy 5×5 boards before trying bigger grids. Check our How to Play guide for a complete walkthrough.
Is there a GridPaw mobile app?
Yes, GridPaw is available on Google Play, and the web version works on any device with a browser. The grid is fully responsive — long-press cells to mark them with paw prints on mobile.
Does my progress save automatically?
Yes, your progress, lives, and current level are saved automatically in your browser via local storage, so you can come back and continue anytime on the same device.
What do the numbered black cells mean?
Each number tells you exactly how many of the 4 adjacent cells (up, down, left, right) must contain a cat. A "0" means none, a "4" means all four. Unnumbered black cells are just walls — they block light but give no clues.
Can I create my own puzzles?
Yes! Visit the Create Puzzle page to design your own Akari grid. The tool validates that your puzzle has exactly one solution, then generates a shareable link.
Does GridPaw have a daily challenge?
Yes! A fresh 10×10 puzzle is generated every day, and weekends (Sat & Sun UTC) feature a 14×14 Weekend Super Challenge. Track your solving streak and earn badges at 3, 7, 14, and 30 consecutive days. Visit the Daily Challenge page to play today's puzzle.
